summary: The Congenital Heart Futures Reauthorization Act of 2024 (Public Law 118-107) amends section 399V-2 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 280g-13) to reauthorize the national congenital heart disease research, surveillance, and awareness program and to impose new reporting and strategic planning requirements on the Secretary of Health and Human Services. The Act redesignates existing subsections (f) and (g) as (g) and (h), respectively, and inserts a new subsection (f) titled “Report and Strategy.” New subsection (f)(1) directs the Secretary, not later than two years after enactment, to submit a report to the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House and the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate that includes: a description of past and present Department of Health and Human Services activities to increase public awareness and knowledge of congenital heart disease, including efforts addressing lifelong patient needs; an assessment of past and present Department activities to increase health care provider education and training regarding congenital heart disease, including lifelong needs; and a description of the current workforce capacity of providers treating adult patients with congenital heart disease. New subsection (f)(2) requires the Secretary, not later than one year after submitting that report, to develop and submit to Congress a strategy for improving public awareness and knowledge and provider education and training with respect to congenital heart disease. The strategy must include findings and recommendations to address public awareness and research gaps and opportunities related to lifelong needs (including long-term health outcomes, quality of life, mental health, and health care utilization); to address workforce shortages of providers treating adult congenital heart disease patients, which may include enhancing fellowship training or continuing education programs; and to foster collaboration and information dissemination across Federal agencies, health care providers, researchers, and patient organizations. In developing the strategy, the Secretary shall consult, as appropriate, with qualified stakeholder groups, including patient organizations, health care professionals, research entities, health insurance providers, accrediting organizations, and relevant Federal agencies (the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the National Institutes of Health, and the Health Resources and Services Administration). Finally, the Act amends redesignated subsection (h) by striking “2020 through 2024” and inserting “2025 through 2029,” thereby extending the authorization of appropriations for the program through fiscal year 2029. The Act contains no new appropriations, imposes no direct spending, and takes effect on November 21, 2024.
